metadata.title: OCR PDF Translator for Scanned Documents
metadata.description: Use OCR to recognize text in scanned PDFs, review the detected layout, translate supported languages, and export the result. Sign-in is required.

intro: Upload a scanned or image-based PDF, recognize its text, review the detected blocks, and translate the content into one of the supported languages before export.
useCases: Scanned research papers, supplier documents, manuals, and other PDFs whose text cannot be selected or copied.
limits: Sign-in is required. Blurry scans, handwriting, complex tables, unusual fonts, and password-protected PDFs may need manual review or preprocessing.

workflow.title: How the OCR translation workflow works
workflow.intro: Use this workflow when the page is an image and ordinary PDF text extraction cannot produce reliable, selectable text.
workflow.step1Description: Sign in, choose the image-based PDF, and select the source and target languages. Use the regular translator instead when the document already contains clean selectable text.
workflow.step2Description: OCR detects text blocks, reading order, tables, and page regions. Scan quality and document structure affect what can be recognized.
workflow.step3Description: Compare the source page with the workbench result. Correct names, numbers, headings, and reading order before relying on a translation.
workflow.step4Description: Translate the reviewed content, inspect the final pages, and generate PDF, Markdown, or HTML output for the next stage of your work.

review.title: What to review
review.description: Check names, dates, measurements, table cells, footnotes, stamps, and text near page edges. Legal, academic, and financial documents should always be compared with the source.

outputs.title: Available outputs
outputs.description: The workbench can generate PDF, Markdown, and HTML. Layout is retained where technically possible, but complex tables, unusual fonts, and low-resolution scans can require editing.

privacy.title: Account and file handling
privacy.description: File processing requires sign-in and tasks are separated by account. Documents and stored objects are normally scheduled for deletion after about seven days, subject to the published privacy policy and legal exceptions.

faq.title: OCR PDF translation questions
faq.q1: When should I use OCR instead of the regular PDF translator?
faq.a1: Use OCR when text cannot be selected or copied because each page is a scan or image. For a digital PDF with embedded text, start with the regular translator.
faq.q2: Can OCR accurately read handwriting and complex tables?
faq.a2: Results vary with image quality, handwriting style, table borders, and reading order. Treat these areas as review points rather than assuming they were reproduced perfectly.
faq.q3: Which formats can I download from the OCR workbench?
faq.a3: After recognition and translation, the workbench can prepare PDF, Markdown, and HTML exports. Review the generated file before publishing or sharing it.
faq.q4: Do I need an account, and how long are files kept?
faq.a4: You must sign in to upload and process files. Documents and related objects are normally retained for about seven days before scheduled deletion, with details and exceptions described in the privacy policy.
